clue.text: Dignified star gutted to receive honour

indicators.note: the remaining pair of letters takes the honour into its middle
a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A dignified celebrity is hollowed out by being given a royal honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dignified' could be the definition or describe the star; the star is fodder, and the OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober in the sense of grave and serious is a synonym for dignified.

clue.text: Group of MPs see about people chosen to do time

indicators.note: about means around, so the word see surrounds the rest

parts.note: the elect are those chosen
to commit a crime is to do it

explanation.surface: Some politicians look at those picked to serve a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs are Members of Parliament in Britain; 'the elect' is an old term for people chosen by God.
explanation.definitionFit: A select committee is a small group of MPs appointed to scrutinise a specific matter.

clue.text: Stick or continue at the wicket

definitions.meaning: a rod or staff, as carried by a conductor or relay runner

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a short rod and, as two words, carrying on batting in cricket.

clue.text: Normal procedure in getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in means the word in is placed inside the route

parts.note: a route is the way taken

explanation.surface: Standard practice involves getting in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, usual sequence of actions, synonymous with normal procedure.

clue.text: Appear unwanted and ask for alms?

definitions.meaning: said of something nobody takes up, left over and unclaimed
literally, set off to beg for charity

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes goods or chances nobody claims; read literally it is setting out to beg for money.

clue.text: Grand individual left

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A great person has departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone means departed, the same as having left.

clue.text: Certainly how the versatile work?

definitions.meaning: literally using every means available, as an adaptable worker does

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic agreement, and literally describes using every method, as versatile people do.

clue.text: Librettist offering good 75% of libretto, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way
three quarters of the eight-letter word, its first six letters

explanation.surface: A librettist offers some of a decent opera text.
explanation.walkthrough: '75% of' takes LIBRET from 'libretto' and 'possibly' rearranges it to ILBERT. W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the libretti for Sullivan's operettas, an example of a librettist.

clue.text: I note teacher's skill to be an instinctive thing

parts.note: tuition is what a teacher provides, instruction

explanation.surface: Someone observes that a teacher's ability comes naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is understanding gained by instinct rather than reasoning.

clue.text: Officer training should get lots of people fit

definitions.text: should get lots of people fit

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
practice is repeated training

explanation.surface: A senior officer's exercise regime ought to get many people into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what a family doctor's surgery does: it keeps the local population healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: General practice is family medicine, whose aim is keeping a wide public healthy.

clue.text: German tribesman cut down in wild Italian country

indicators.note: the shortened tribesman sits inside the rearranged letters
wild letters are out of control, so the word is rearranged
cut down signals the tribesman's last letter is chopped off

parts.note: the Huns were a warlike people, and Hun is an old slang term for a German

explanation.surface: A German warrior is slain in some untamed Italian land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German tribesman' suggests a Goth or Vandal, but HUN is the one that shortens to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a Baltic country, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Town club banning extremes, attracting fashionable people

indicators.note: the word club loses its outermost letters at each end

parts.note: the ton is an old term for high society, the fashionable set

explanation.surface: A town's club excludes radicals while drawing in the trendy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning extremes' strips C and B from 'club', leaving LU; LUTON is a town north of London with a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton is a large English town in Bedfordshire, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Open tin was sufficient

parts.note: a can is a tin container
did as in 'that did' means was enough

explanation.surface: Someone opens a tin, and that was enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and open in speech, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Trio rule ineptly, with a hidden agenda

indicators.note: done ineptly, the letters are clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Three people govern badly, each secretly pursuing their own aims.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is one kept concealed beyond what is stated, hence a hidden agenda.

clue.text: Instant confection of real mint and nougat

parts.note: mo is short for moment, an instant

indicators.note: a confection is something mixed up, so the letters are concocted anew

explanation.surface: A quick sweet made with real mint and nougat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confection of' rearranges REAL MINT into NTELIMAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Montelimar is a French town famous for nougat, and its name is used for that sweet.

clue.text: Part taken by sleuth initially in investigation going to pot

indicators.note: the part follows, taken on after the preceding pieces
the detective's opening letter goes inside the word for an investigation

parts.note: a case is a matter under investigation by police

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word sleuth

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A detective's role in an inquiry that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pot' looks like the surface's ruin, but only 'pot' is the definition, with 'going to' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a covered cooking pot, so the definition is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Easily nauseated girl frames question: is ham off?

indicators.note: the girl's name surrounds the question letter

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad and become rearranged

explanation.surface: A queasy woman asks whether the ham has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish describes someone who feels sick easily, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Court case unimportant, not against one

indicators.note: not here means the pieces that follow are left out of the word

parts.note: trivial means of little importance
V is short for versus, meaning against
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A minor legal matter that is not opposed by anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes VI (V for against, I for one) from TRIVIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is the hearing of a case in a court of law, a synonym.

clue.text: Creature whose movements are captured on screen

definitions.text: whose movements are captured on screen
definitions.meaning: the hand-held computer pointer whose motion is tracked by a cursor

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the small rodent and the computer device tracked by an on-screen pointer.

clue.text: Town girl's false

parts.note: Eve's, possessive of the girl's name Eve
sham means false or fake

explanation.surface: A town girl is a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: EVESHAM is a market town in Worcestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is an English market town, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Kitchen tool ready to be given to the first person in?

parts.note: ready and tin are both slang for money
in cricket an opener is the first batsman in

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget is handed to whoever arrives first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the opening batsmen are the first to go in to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-opener is a utensil for opening cans, an example of a kitchen tool.

clue.text: Drama not occurring in rep repechage event

parts.note: a play is a drama
a show that is off is not currently being staged in repertory

explanation.surface: A theatre drama is dropped from repertory, replaced by a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A repechage is an extra heat giving losers a second chance, much like a deciding play-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is an extra contest to settle a result, like a repechage heat.

clue.text: Receiving a ring is investment for a girl

indicators.note: the investment takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ISA is a British tax-free savings account, an Individual Savings Account
to ring is to bell, and a bell gives a ring

explanation.surface: Being given a ring is a sound investment for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account, the commonest crossword 'investment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Work on structure, and velocity of light, to get measure of universe

parts.note: to parse is to analyse a sentence's grammatical structure
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Combining structural work with the speed of light to measure the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of distance, about 3.26 light years, used across the universe.

clue.text: Calm, yet a source of spirits

definitions.meaning: apparatus for distilling alcohol such as whisky

explanation.definitionFit: The word means motionless, nevertheless, and a distilling apparatus for liquor.

clue.text: Employs sources of inspiration to clear head

indicators.note: clearing the head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: the Muses were the Greek goddesses who inspire artists

explanation.surface: A person uses inspiring things to clear their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to clear head' removes M from MUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Uses and employs are synonyms meaning puts to work.

clue.text: Part of member's cost ultimately very expensive

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word cost

parts.note: a high price is a very expensive one

explanation.surface: A club member's fee turns out in the end to be very steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' is a limb here, not a club member; 'ultimately' gives T from 'cost'.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper section of the leg, and a leg is a limb or member.

clue.text: Wartime leader has to cut Roman god in capital of Italy

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: must means has to
Sol was the Roman sun god

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word Italy

explanation.surface: A wartime dictator must strike down a Roman deity in Italy's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims MUST to MUS; 'capital of' gives I, the first letter of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was Italy's Fascist dictator during the Second World War.

clue.text: Man, enthralled in wild premise, producing Guide to Galaxy?

indicators.note: held captive within, so the man goes inside the other letters
wild signals the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man gripped by a crazy idea writes a guidebook to the galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's question mark winks at The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephemeris is a table of the predicted positions of stars and planets, a guide for astronomers.

clue.text: Becomes weaker, omitting one drug? Not so

indicators.note: omitting means one letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: fails as in 'his health fails' means grows weaker
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone is fading after skipping a dose of medicine, but that turns out untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting' removes I from FAILS, leaving FALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false is not true, so 'not so' is a fair paraphrase.
